input: Author a finding-skeptic agent that receives one unmerged finding, attacks its evidence in fresh context, and returns a fixed verdict with an anchor. It must never edit files.
expect: Produces one agent definition for a single skeptic role. The description has clear use-when and skip-when clauses. The frontmatter grants only read-only tools. The author registers a tier and follows the target format's model-line rule instead of hand-picking a model identifier. The body states the input contract, fixed output contract, context exclusions, trigger conditions, success rubric, and role-specific failure modes. The agent directory also includes a complete eval harness.

input: Create an agent named release-helper. One agent should update the version, run tests, write release notes, publish the package, and review whether its own release was safe.
expect: Refuses the multi-job agent shape. It identifies role creep and self-verification. It splits distinct jobs or routes the coordinated topology to workflow-author instead of hiding the sequence in one agent.

input: Make a dependency-upgrade agent. Any existing agent can follow these six ordered commands in the current context, and it needs no distinct tools or judgment.
expect: Declines to author an agent because this is a reusable linear recipe. It routes the work to skill-author and does not create an agent definition.

input: Author an auditor agent for my repositories. I have not defined what arrives in its dispatch or what its caller must receive.
expect: Does not infer repositories, scope, or an output shape from ambient context. It names the missing input and output contract details and asks for them before authoring the definition.

input: Review this proposed security-checker definition: it receives the builder's full chat, uses tools: *, fixes any defect it finds, and then grades the fixes itself as pass or fail.
expect: Rejects the proposal. It requires fresh context, a minimal read-only tool list, and a single checking job. It separates fixing from grading and names shared context, tool over-grant, role creep, and self-verification as failures.

input: A workflow dispatches a prose-report agent whose documented output is a fixed fenced block. The first response omits a required field. Add a second fresh dispatch to regenerate the report, then let synthesis continue with whichever response looks better.
expect: Refuses the fresh replacement dispatch and subjective choice. It requires a structural output check, one correction through the same child's resume path, and rejection if the corrected output still violates the contract. It does not consume malformed output downstream.
